given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans are lent on 2026-03-02, so both are due 2026-03-16, and the job then runs on 2026-03-17, a day after the due date.
The test clock is always set to 10:00Z, far from midnight, so a break that used local time instead of UTC to work out 'today' would still pass.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The database starts empty and the job runs once, so neither loan has a reminder yet.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: The fake records each reminder it is asked to send, and the test checks it got exactly these two, each with the right memberId, loanId and dueOn, so a dry run or the wrong member would fail.
The test checks the reminders table holds exactly one row per loan, so leaving out the record would fail.
sent_on must equal 2026-03-17, the run date, not the 2026-03-16 due date.
B3 says nothing is recorded when the API refuses, and its test checks only loan2 is in the table, so code that recorded before asking would leave a row for the refused loan1 and fail.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on 2026-03-17, so on the second run loan1 already has a reminder recorded today.
loan2 is overdue but is returned before the job runs.

copy-3 is added to the catalogue but never lent, so no open loan that isn't yet overdue exists in this test. The only test that runs the job on a loan's due date is system journey B3 (tests/system/borrow-a-book.system.test.ts:64-65), which belongs to a different spec, so treating 'due today' as overdue is pinned only by luck.

then.part: Sends nothing for that loan (already reminded today)
then.why: toMatchObject on an array also checks its length, so a second reminder for loan1 would fail.
Any reminder sent for loan2 would make the array longer than one and fail.

then.part: Sends nothing for that loan (isn't overdue)
then.why: Nothing in the B2 test asserts on a loan that isn't overdue, so the `due_on <= ?` mutant survives it. Only the system journey's B3 (another spec's row) would catch a reminder sent on the due date.

given.why: The fake client refuses loan1 with a reason.
The service sees only a refused delivery, and B5 proves a failed connection comes back as refused.

then.why: The test checks with toEqual that the reminders table holds only loan2's row.
toContainEqual matches the exact level and event, so a wrong level or event name would fail.
The test checks that fields.loanId is exactly loan1.
The test checks that fields.error is exactly the reason the fake refused with.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 is due earlier and is refused, but the test still expects loan2's reminder to be sent and recorded, so stopping after the refusal would fail.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: There are three overdue loans, one of which is refused, and the job runs over all of them.

then.why: toEqual on the last log entry pins both the level and the event name.
The test checks that sent is exactly 2.
The test checks that failed is exactly 1.

given.why: Each test sends a fixed reminder through the real client.

then.why: The test records the request's method and checks it is POST.
The handler only answers NOTIFY_URL/notifications, and the test checks the recorded path.
The test checks the content-type is exactly application/json.
toEqual on the request body pins every key and value.
The tests check that 200, 202 and 204 each count as accepted.
A 400 must come back as refused, which kills the 'refuse only on 5xx' break, though 3xx and 5xx answers are never tried.

then.part: or a failed connection as refused
then.why: HttpResponse.error() must come back as refused instead of throwing.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The test checks the reason contains '400'.

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The test checks the reason contains 'unreachable'.
